prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: CRESUM Reverse-Grip (SUPINATED) FRONT Lat Pulldown, male START phase only. Produce a new draft consistent with the references, not a comparison or montage.

IMAGE 1 supplies the exact CRESUM male identity, blue-gray T-shirt, dark shorts, white socks, light gray trainers, realistic fit physique, dark gray selectorized machine, seat/thigh rollers, camera/crop, lighting and white studio background. Preserve these, including the pelvis, legs, shoes and contact with the machine. Remove its small double neutral handle completely.
IMAGE 2 supplies the chosen chrome pulldown bar's shape: a long straight central shaft, matching angled outer ends, matching inner knurled zones and a compact central swivel collar with one upright eyelet. Use this same manufactured rigid symmetric bar, reprojected into image 1's three-quarter side/rear camera.

CHANGE THE EXERCISE TO REVERSE UNDERHAND GRIP. BOTH hands hold the STRAIGHT INNER knurled areas, one on each side of the central collar, approximately shoulder width or comfortably just inside shoulder width. The long angled ends extend outward EMPTY; neither hand is placed on an outer angled section. This is not the wide overhand version and not a neutral parallel-handle grip.

Supination is the key: the anatomical left and right PALMS FACE THE ATHLETE, backward toward his face/chest, as in an underhand chin-up. The backs of both hands face generally toward the weight tower. Both forearms are supinated naturally and consistently, not one palm facing inward and the other outward. Where the camera can see a palmar surface, show the fleshy palm/thumb-side anatomy and flexor wrist rather than painting a dorsal hand over it. Do not rotate separate hands toward the camera merely to display them. Allow honest near/far occlusion.
Each proportional adult hand securely wraps the same straight bar with four curled fingers and an opposing wrapped thumb. Left and right thumbs have their true anatomical positions. Each thumb closes the grasp naturally toward the inner side; do not mirror a right hand twice. Fingers contact metal without intersection. Wrists remain approximately straight relative to the forearms, no sharp backward bend, sideways kink or elbow dislocation. Do not twist the upper arms or entire torso to create supination.

START pose: arms reach overhead and a little forward, elbows almost extended without forced lockout. Hand spacing is comfortable, much closer than the outer ends of the long bar; upper arms follow naturally from the shoulders. The bar is above and in front of the head, under the original high pulley, its left-right axis perpendicular to the athlete's forward-facing direction. Both shoulder blades can rotate/elevate naturally with this overhead reach; do not pin them down or exaggerate a shrug. Natural bone lengths and shoulder proportions.

Man sits facing the tower, head/torso/pelvis aligned, modest stable backward lean like image 1, no trunk twist, rib flare or exaggerated lumbar arch. Head in line with spine, gaze toward machine. Hips fully seated, both thighs under and touching the rollers, knees naturally bent, both soles on the same floor plane. Preserve the reference's near shoe forward and far shoe partly occluded beneath the seat, with coherent shoe direction. No foot perched on a frame rail.

One central closed steel carabiner passes through the bar collar's single eyelet, connected to the cable terminal and small black rubber stop above. The taut cable connects back to the unchanged high pulley's real exit. Collar at the true midpoint, no added chain or floating connector. All parts share the same 3D perspective; do not separately rotate the bar for a front-on product view. Preserve the reference machine frame, guide rods, pulleys and the entire resting START stack, including original total plate count and yellow selector position. No raised stack in START.

Premium semi-realistic 3D educational rendering with natural skin, detailed hands, restrained muscles, plausible clothing folds, coherent chrome reflections and soft contact shadows. Portrait composition, entire machine/base, character and bar ends visible with white margin. No text, logos, arrows, inset or muscle coloring. Only START, not the downward pull. Priority: visibly genuine bilateral underhand grip on the inner straight bar, neutral wrists, natural overhead reach, mechanically connected cable and unchanged seated support.
productionChoice: Existing chrome bar, underhand grip on straight inner portions at comfortable near-shoulder spacing; draft presentation only, no canonical catalog attachment/width change.
